requests.description: Must contain exactly one Digital Credentials API request.

protocol.description: The DC API protocol. Only the signed variant `openid4vp-v1-signed` is supported.

request.description: The signed OID4VP request object (a JAR), as a compact JWS. It MUST have `typ` header `oauth-authz-req+jwt`, be signed with ES256 by a key whose JWK is registered on your OAuth Application, and carry the OID4VP request claims: `iss` (equal to `client_id`), `aud` (the Proof presentation issuer), `client_id`, `response_type` (`vp_token`), `response_mode` (`dc_api`), `scope`, `login_hint`, and `nonce`. For the intermediary flow, also include `expected_origins`. To let AI agents poll for the result instead, set `expected_origins` to exactly the agents trust list (`/.well-known/agents-trust-list` on this API host) and omit `response_uri`.

return_uri.description: Optional. Enables the x401 intermediary return channel (https://x401.proof.com/spec/latest/#return-channel). When present, Proof POSTs the Verifiable Credential Presentation to this URI instead of the request object's `response_uri`. Its origin must be listed in the request object's `expected_origins`, and the request object must not itself specify a `response_uri`. Omit it when the request object's `expected_origins` is the agents trust list: Proof then keeps the result for the calling agent to poll at `result_polling_uri`.

request_uri.description: A link to the Proof-hosted flow where the End-User authorizes the Verifiable Credential Presentation.

result_polling_uri.description: Only present when the request object's `expected_origins` is the agents trust list and `return_uri` is omitted. Poll this URI with the same `agentic` access token to retrieve the Verifiable Credential Presentation once the End-User completes the flow.

status.description: `pending` while the End-User has not completed the flow, `completed` once the presentation is available.

credential_result.description: Only present when `status` is `completed`. Use it as the `credential_result` member of an x401 Result Artifact (https://x401.proof.com/spec/latest/).

vp_token.description: The OID4VP `vp_token`, as Proof would have posted it to a `response_uri`.

issuer_signature.description: The base64url signature segment of the Issuer-signed JWT, to splice back into the first `~`-separated part of the SD-JWT.

kb_signature.description: The base64url signature segment of the Key Binding JWT, to splice back into the last `~`-separated part of the SD-JWT.

error_description.description: Human-readable detail about the error, for developers.

get.description: Initiates an OID4VP Verifiable Credential Presentation request for the End-User identified by their Proof session, or by `login_hint` when they are not signed in. Returns a 302 redirect to the Proof-hosted flow where the End-User authorizes the presentation. Once complete, Proof returns the Verifiable Credential Presentation according to `response_mode`: for `fragment`, the `vp_token` is appended as a URL fragment on a redirect back to `redirect_uri`; for `direct_post`, the `vp_token` is POSTed to `response_uri`.

parameters.name: client_id
parameters.description: Your Proof OAuth Application Client ID.

parameters.name: response_type
parameters.description: The method used to return the Verifiable Credential Presentation. Only `vp_token` is supported.

parameters.name: response_mode
parameters.description: How the Verifiable Credential Presentation will be returned to the Verifier. Use `fragment` to have the `vp_token` returned as a URL fragment on a redirect to `redirect_uri`, or `direct_post` to have Proof POST the `vp_token` to `response_uri`.

parameters.name: redirect_uri
parameters.description: Required when `response_mode` is `fragment`; not permitted otherwise. The redirect URI at which the Verifiable Credential Presentation will be returned as a URL fragment. Must match a redirect URI registered on your OAuth Application.

parameters.name: response_uri
parameters.description: Required when `response_mode` is `direct_post`; not permitted otherwise. The URI to which Proof will POST the Verifiable Credential Presentation. Must match a redirect URI registered on your OAuth Application.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Space-separated list of scopes that translate to DCQL queries.

parameters.name: login_hint
parameters.description: The email address associated with the End-User you're requesting Verifiable Credential presentation from. Optional: an End-User signed in to Proof takes precedence over `login_hint`. When omitted, the End-User is sent through login first if they are not already signed in.

parameters.name: nonce
parameters.description: Opaque client-generated value bound to the presentation response to prevent replay.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Opaque value echoed back on the redirect to maintain state between the request and the callback.

parameters.name: transaction_data
parameters.description:
Space-separated base64url-encoded JSON objects (a JSON array in a signed request object). Each object carries transaction details the Verifier is asking the End-User to authorize, with the shape: 

- `type` (string, required): one of `urn:proof:params:vc:transaction-data:session-data`, `urn:proof:params:vc:transaction-data:payment-itemized:v1`, `urn:proof:params:vc:transaction-data:wire-instructions:v1`, or `urn:proof:params:vc:transaction-data:payment-mandate:v1`.
- `credential_ids` (array of strings, required): must be a single-element array matching the credential ID targeted by `scope` (currently `proof_id_default`).
- `payload` (object, required): type-specific fields authorized by the End-User.

Example (decoded): `{"type":"urn:proof:params:vc:transaction-data:session-data","credential_ids":["proof_id_default"],"payload":{"ip_address":"203.0.113.0","device_id":"device-1989"}}`.

Location.description: URL of the Proof-hosted flow where the End-User authorizes the Verifiable Credential Presentation.

post.summary: Hand off an x401 Verifiable Credential Presentation request
post.description:
Accepts an x401 payload (https://x401.proof.com/spec/latest/#x401-payload) that wraps a Digital Credentials API request (https://www.w3.org/TR/digital-credentials/#DC-API) using the `openid4vp-v1-signed` protocol, and processes it as an OID4VP presentation request for the End-User identified by the `login_hint` claim of the signed request object. When the request carries a Proof access token issued to an End-User in the `Authorization: Bearer` header, that End-User is used instead of `login_hint`, and an invalid token is rejected with `invalid_token`. 

The real OID4VP request is carried inside the signed request object at `credential_requirements.digital.requests[0].data.request`: a compact JWS with `typ` header `oauth-authz-req+jwt`, signed with ES256 by a key whose JWK is registered on your OAuth Application. Your `client_id` is conveyed by the request object's `iss`/`client_id` claims. Its `response_mode` must be `dc_api`. It must carry an `exp` claim at most one hour ahead and a unique `jti` claim; a request object is accepted once. 

On success Proof returns a `request_uri` suitable for presenting to the End-User via their AI agent. Supply a top-level `return_uri` to use the x401 intermediary return channel (https://x401.proof.com/spec/latest/#return-channel); its origin must appear in the request object's `expected_origins`.

AI agents that cannot receive the presentation themselves omit `return_uri` and send an access token with the `agentic` scope. This requires the request object's `expected_origins` to be the agents trust list. Proof then also returns a `result_polling_uri` the agent polls with the same access token.

parameters.name: Authorization
parameters.description: Optional `Bearer` access token issued by Proof to the End-User, with the `mcp.read` or `agentic` scope. When present, the transaction is created for that End-User instead of `login_hint`. Required, with the `agentic` scope, to receive a `result_polling_uri`.

get.summary: Poll an x401 Verifiable Credential Presentation result
get.description: Returns the Verifiable Credential Presentation of an x401 handoff created without `return_uri`, once the End-User completes the flow. The End-User may take several minutes (identity verification). Poll no faster than the `Retry-After` header of a `202` response. A pending result expires after one hour, a completed result five minutes after completion. Only the End-User of the access token that created the handoff can read the result; any other caller receives `404`.

parameters.name: Authorization
parameters.description: `Bearer` access token with the `agentic` scope, issued to the End-User who created the handoff.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The transaction identifier ending the `result_polling_uri` returned by the handoff.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before polling again.

post.summary: Fetch the detached signatures of an x401 Verifiable Credential Presentation
post.description:
Presentations delivered through x401 to an organization billed by invoice, with no card or bank account on file, omit the signature segment of both the Issuer-signed JWT and the Key Binding JWT. The Key Binding JWT header carries a critical `proof.com#sig-1` parameter whose value is the `id` to send here. Authenticate with a `private_key_jwt` client assertion from the OAuth Application that requested the presentation, with `aud` set to this endpoint URL. 

When the transaction is not yet paid, the first call answers `402` with x402 payment requirements (https://www.x402.org) for the transaction price; repeat the request with the `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` header to settle and receive the signatures. A `409` means the transaction is still being finalized: retry after the `Retry-After` delay. Records expire one hour after the presentation.

PAYMENT-REQUIRED.description: Base64 x402 payment requirements; the body carries the same JSON.

example.error: Payment required to access this resource

example.error_description: the transaction is still being finalized, retry shortly

id.description: The value of the `proof.com#sig-1` header parameter of the Key Binding JWT.

client_assertion.description: A `private_key_jwt` assertion signed by a key registered on your OAuth Application, with `aud` set to this endpoint URL.
